﻿# 从博主到年入$2100万的媒体科技巨头

## 冷启动：2001年用33k调制解调器建网站

Armed with 386 PC and squeaky 33k modem。

Ben launched first online publication back in 2001，while in high school。

Satirical student site called Seuch Times。

Created great content，built audience，monetized with t-shirt sales！

Was hooked。

Experience of creating content with and for community。

Connecting with niche audiences and turning into business planted seed for everything came later。

After decade managing digital projects at top agencies in London。

Moved to Vancouver and continued work in digital project management。

Decided to launch blog about it。

Helping people get into and succeed as digital project managers。

Meant to be side project。

Lead-gen tool for ebook planned to sell but never published。

Site slowly grew。

Over many years，realized much bigger opportunity：

Build network of practitioner-led publications。

Each serving specific niche of modern work。

That side project became flagship brand，The Digital Project Manager。

Foundation for Black & White Zebra (BWZ)。

BWZ bootstrapped，profitable，growing。

15+ niche media brands。

Including People Managing People，The Product Manager。

Millions of monthly visitors。

Strong foundation of trust and utility with audiences。

Right now，building two new things incredibly excited about：

**Revstacks**：Monetization and AdTech platform for B2B publishers、creators、professional communities。

**Revleads**：B2B SaaS demand-gen platform helps marketers reach in-market buyers through trusted，high-converting editorial environments。

Grown BWZ from zero to $21M+ annual revenue。

$9M in EBIT last year。

Onboarded 220+ advertisers。

Now power monetization for 10 publisher partners through Revstacks。

## 反直觉：他把成功藏起来，结果害了自己

Firstly，build brand early。

Not enough to be good — people need to know you're good。

For too long，were best-kept secret in B2B media。

That hurt in hiring and in sales。

If could do over，be much more intentional about telling story while built。

Not just once had something to show。

Lot of early-stage founders focus too much on idea and not enough on execution。

He's been guilty of that too。

Has notebooks full of great ideas went nowhere。

What matters isn't how good idea sounds。

Whether can turn into something useful。

Whether can do it consistently。

For him，everything changed when started thinking like project manager：

1. Set vision — where trying to go？
2. Define success — what does good look like？
3. Work backward — what has to be true for that to happen？
4. Break into steps — then make those steps smaller。
5. Keep going — momentum compounds。

## 暴击：COVID期间差点挂了，亏了1/3收入

One major challenge came during COVID。

Scaled rapidly — from small，collocated team to globally distributed across multiple time zones。

Grew headcount，but not always in right way。

Hired lot of people，some managers。

Many weren't senior or experienced enough to lead at level needed。

Trying to scale before stabilizing foundation。

Would do differently next time：

One time zone，better onboarding，far more intentional leadership hiring。

Because of leadership gap，period where producing ton of content — but wrong content，done wrong way。

Didn't match user intent，wasn't high enough quality，wasn't aligned with search demand。

Lost steam fast — and at one point，lost nearly third of revenue。

That was wake-up call。

In trying to grow，lost track of core — audience insight，delivering real value。

Now，stays in weeds where matters。

Makes sure high-level strategy filters down through org。

Digs into frontline work，not to micromanage，but ensure pointed in right direction。

Hard lesson as CEO：

Execution is everything。

Good ideas easy。

Great execution rare。

Had moments where vision clear，but team、process、timing wasn't right — and idea died。

Now ruthless about attaching plans、capacity、accountability to every major initiative。

##  punchline：严肃的事情也可以很有趣

Didn't come from digital media background。

Turned out to be advantage。

Wasn't constrained by how things "supposed" to be done。

Just focused on solving real problems and doing in way felt clear、human、fun。

That's one of core philosophies：

**Serious things can be fun。**

Business doesn't have to be boring。

Work doesn't have to feel like chore。

If understand something deeply enough，can simplify it。

If can simplify，can make engaging。

That's where magic happens。

Most of business — content、community、even ad sales — grew out of relationships built by being useful and honest。

Biggest advertisers came inbound because already helping future customers do jobs better。

And have strong opinions (lightly held)。

Need conviction to start something。

But also need humility to evolve it。

Stay close to problem，be willing to change solution as learn more。
